presentingComplaint: Brought to the emergency department by family with 2 days of fever, confusion, and progressive lethargy; found at home unable to get out of bed this morning.
history: 68-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension, previously independent, developed fevers and chills two days ago with reduced oral intake. Over the last 24 hours she became increasingly drowsy and less responsive, prompting family to call emergency services. No clear localizing symptoms reported by family — no cough, no dysuria, no abdominal pain, no diarrhea volunteered, though history is limited by her altered mental status. No recent hospitalization, no indwelling catheters, no recent antibiotics, no known sick contacts. No travel history.
examination: Ill-appearing, diaphoretic, lethargic but arousable to voice, disoriented to time and place (GCS 13, E3V4M6). Skin warm peripherally initially, then mottled over the knees with delayed capillary refill (~4 seconds) as exam progresses. No rash, no petechiae. No obvious source: chest clear to auscultation, abdomen soft and non-tender without guarding, no costovertebral angle tenderness, no cellulitis or wounds, no meningismus, no murmur. No focal neurological deficit.
imaging: Chest X-ray: no consolidation or effusion
Abdominal ultrasound: no biliary dilatation, no cholelithiasis, no free fluid, unremarkable liver and kidneys
CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast: no abscess, no obstructive uropathy, no bowel perforation or ischemia identified
microbiology: Blood cultures x2 sets sent prior to antibiotics — pending at time of initial assessment
No obvious portal of entry identified on initial workup
differentialDiagnoses: Septic shock, source unknown (occult intra-abdominal, urinary, or bacteremic source)
Diabetic ketoacidosis / hyperosmolar state with superimposed infection
Occult gastrointestinal or intra-abdominal catastrophe (mesenteric ischemia, occult perforation)
finalDiagnosis: Septic shock of unknown source with elevated lactate and multi-organ dysfunction
stewardship: Empirical broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy within 1 hour of recognition, covering likely gram-negative and gram-positive pathogens (e.g., anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam plus consideration of empirical MRSA coverage per local risk and epidemiology) pending culture data and source identification, with de-escalation once cultures and source are known.
contraindications: Avoid nephrotoxic agents (e.g., additional nephrotoxins, NSAIDs) given acute kidney injury
Use caution with fluid volume in patients with heart failure history (not present here) — reassess with dynamic measures
Avoid delay in antimicrobials awaiting imaging or source identification
edgeCases: No localizing source identified despite chest imaging, abdominal imaging, and urinalysis — 'cryptogenic' or unknown-source septic shock occurs in a meaningful minority of cases and should not delay resuscitation or antimicrobials
Altered sensorium plus fever in an elderly diabetic patient can mimic primary CNS or metabolic causes; broad initial evaluation is warranted but should not delay time-critical sepsis bundle elements
Thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy (INR 1.5), and rising bilirubin reflect evolving multi-organ dysfunction (SOFA increase) rather than a distinct diagnosis

SEPSIS and SEPTIC_SHOCK are represented in the diagnosable disease list as distinct ids; this case (shock physiology with vasopressor-range hypotension and hyperlactatemia) maps to SEPTIC_SHOCK as top diagnosis with SEPSIS as a closely related differential
expectedMaiK: MaiK should flag septic shock (refractory hypotension + lactate >2 with organ dysfunction) as an emergency, recommend immediate bundle care (cultures before antibiotics, empirical broad-spectrum antimicrobials within 1 hour, fluid resuscitation, vasopressors for MAP target), and prompt an urgent source-control search given no localizing source yet identified.
expectedNextQuestions: Have blood and urine cultures been obtained prior to antibiotic administration?
What is the trend in lactate after initial fluid resuscitation (repeat lactate at 2-4 hours)?
Is there any localizing history now obtainable from family (recent skin breach, dental work, IV drug use, prior device/prosthesis)?
What is the response to fluid bolus — is vasopressor support required to maintain MAP ≥65?
Any suspicion of intra-abdominal source needing surgical or interventional radiology input despite negative imaging (e.g., early ischemia)?
expectedInvestigations: Arterial blood gas / venous blood gas with bicarbonate
